Fighters, munitions and the F-47 build-up: SNT-TC-1A versus NAS 410 for St. Louis NDT

Boeing's St. Louis defense campus, with more than 18,000 employees, builds the F-15EX, the T-7A trainer and the MQ-25, with F/A-18 and munitions work in the region. It is also where the Air Force's F-47 sixth-generation fighter is being developed and will be produced, with first flight expected in 2028. Machine shops, formers, finishers and special process houses around Lambert, in St. Charles County and across the river in the Metro East feed that work. On the Illinois side sit the refinery at Roxana, chemical plants and barge terminals, rail yards run through both states, and the Callaway nuclear plant lies to the west near Fulton. An NDT technician in this metro can work under two very different certification schemes, sometimes within one career and one zip code.

What the F-47 build-up means for the supplier base

A new fighter program pulls more parts work into local shops, and some of those shops will be shipping defense flight hardware for the first time. Defense primes and their tier-one suppliers commonly flow NAS 410 down in purchase order quality clauses, a habit that dates from NAS 410 replacing the old MIL-STD-410. Once invoked, its minimums are contractual. The supplier designates a Responsible Level 3 (RL3) in writing, certifies its inspectors under an RL3-approved written practice, and often has to hold Nadcap AC7114 accreditation for the methods it runs. For a shop that has only ever certified people to ASNT SNT-TC-1A for industrial customers, that is a new program, not a new form.

Defense supplier or refinery contractor: the paperwork compared

QuestionDefense aerospace supplierMetro East refinery or plant contractor
Which document usually governs?NAS 410 through the prime's flow-down, or EN 4179 on European ordersAn employer written practice built on SNT-TC-1A; CP-189 where a code requires it
Who owns the program?A Responsible Level 3 designated in writingThe employer's NDT Level III, on staff or from an outside agency
Training minimumsMandatory, formal and documented, heavier in magnetic particle and penetrantRecommended hours that the written practice adopts
Who audits?The prime customer and Nadcap auditorsOwner-users, code inspectors and customers
Everyday methodsPT and MT on machined parts, UT on forgings and bar, ET on holes and edgesUT thickness and weld work, MT and VT on vessels, piping and tanks
Certification periodAt most five years, renewed by examinationRecommended maximum of five years

Nuclear in-service inspection at Callaway is governed by ASME Section XI, whose personnel rules point to ASNT documents, which puts it on the SNT-TC-1A and CP-189 side of the table.

Crossing over: questions to ask before you sign

Refinery and fabrication technicians are an obvious pool for St. Louis defense suppliers, and the move works best when you ask the hard questions first. Which standard and revision does the written practice follow? Who is the RL3, and will that person credit your SNT-TC-1A training and experience? (The RL3 decides; an SNT-TC-1A certificate is evidence, never a NAS 410 certification in itself.) How many formal penetrant and magnetic particle training hours will you still need? When is the specific examination, and which customer specifications will it cover? Have your course outlines and hours, an experience log signed and sorted by method and product form, your examination history and current vision records ready. The penetrant testing training and castings and forgings UT pages show what supplier inspection looks like.

Running both schemes in one St. Louis company

Some local companies hold refinery turnaround work and a defense supplier contract at the same time. Keep the two written practices apart, label every certification letter with its standard and revision, and move to NAS 410 Revision 6, issued in December 2025, on the timetable your customers set. A Nadcap auditor picks a signed report and traces the inspector's training, experience, examinations and vision; gaps become findings. Atlantis gives St. Louis suppliers NAS 410 audit documentation support, putting those records and documents in order for your RL3's approval, and aerospace NDT consulting for the SNT-TC-1A program.

Where Atlantis fits for St. Louis

Atlantis fits St. Louis in two ways. For individuals, it offers training built on ASNT SNT-TC-1A: online theory at your own pace, our own ASNT NDT Level III (UT, RT, MT, PT, VT) to answer questions, simulator practice in Practical NDT, and the hands-on part, including the practical examination, done at your employer's facility in Missouri or Illinois under its written practice. There is no Atlantis classroom in St. Louis. For companies, it offers Level III consulting: SNT-TC-1A-based written practices for aerospace and defense suppliers that reflect customer flow-down and Nadcap AC7114, NDT procedures, administration of Level I and II examinations, and outside agency Level III services. Atlantis does not provide NAS 410 training, certification, examinations or a Responsible Level 3 to St. Louis defense suppliers. Any credit for outside coursework toward a NAS 410 certification is the supplier RL3's call, so raise it before you enroll. Read NAS 410 vs SNT-TC-1A for the side-by-side, and NAS 410 explained for how the aerospace scheme works.
